passages.note: House Third Reading vote page shows Dunn voting Y on HB2492, a single-subject voter-registration/citizenship bill.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship.
passages.note: Enacted bill text (Chapter 99) requires documentary proof of citizenship to register, rejecting applications that lack it.

rows.reasoning: Dunn, then a State Representative, voted Y on HB2492 (2022), a single-subject voter-registration and citizenship-verification bill whose operative text requires that registration applications be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship and be rejected if they are not, matching "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote." His earlier-chamber vote counts for his current Senate seat under the same-legislature rule (V5).
